summary:
SHK: Artemis Aero-Trajectory Simulator
Summary
We developed the SHK Simulator, an educational tool that combines a rocket trajectory physics model with AIGC visual interactions. It addresses the challenge of making deep space exploration's complex physical mechanics intuitive for the general public by utilizing simplified aerodynamics and real-time trajectory calculations. This solution is crucial because it transforms dry mathematical logic into an immersive, interactive experience. By visualizing the hard-core science behind the ARTEMIS mission, we aim to lower the barrier to aerospace education and ignite teenagers' passion for aerospace engineering and space exploration.
details:
Project Details

How it works:

The SHK project builds a fundamental mechanics and aerodynamics environment using code. Users can adjust parameters like the Center of Pressure, thrust, and launch angle through an interactive interface, while the system calculates and displays the trajectory changes in real-time.

Benefits and Expected Impact:

Traditional physics and calculus have a high learning curve. SHK visualizes these hardcore concepts, allowing middle school students to intuitively understand the dynamic principles of rocket launches. We expect this to significantly lower the threshold for aerospace science popularization.

Tools, Coding Languages, and Hardware:

We completed the core conceptual design and layout on an iPad Pro. Python was used for physical formula calculations and data modeling. Additionally, we utilized AIGC (Generative AI) tools to create a Future Bass sci-fi background soundtrack and UI visual elements, building an immersive space atmosphere.

Creative Elements and Considerations:

Our core creativity lies in "wrapping science in art." During development, our main consideration was balancing the "accuracy of physical data" with the "fun of user experience." We drew inspiration from physical model debugging, transforming real-world engineering troubleshooting into engaging user challenges.
